brief.idea: two cousins solve the mystery of who keeps moving the lucky cat in their grandmother's shop
brief.setting: a small shop on a busy street in Seoul, today

premise.title: The Walking Lucky Cat
premise.logline: Jina must catch whatever moves her grandmother's lucky cat before nine in the morning, or Minho will be blamed and banned from the shop forever.
premise.theme: The shop's luck was never the cat on the shelf; it was a cat who had everyone exactly where she wanted them.
premise.hook: Halmoni sets the big lucky cat facing the door and turns to the kettle — in that one second the cat faces the wall, and nothing in the shop has moved except a red collar.
premise.stakes: Minho loses the shop and his snack shelf, and Halmoni is left believing her luck walked out on her.
tools: a ticking clock: before Halmoni unlocks the shop at nine
dramatic irony: we watch Nabi nudge the cat while the cousins argue about crumbs
a false victory: they 'catch' Minho and the evidence in the same minute
the it-cannot-get-worse beat: Minho is banned, then the whole shelf of lucky cats goes over
a cliffhanger: the morning after the stakeout the cat has moved again — and the red door was bolted
premise.gag: Minho's backpack: every time he digs for evidence a different snack falls out — rice cake, dried squid, chocolate — and he eats it before Jina can look.
clues: A white hair with an orange patch, stuck to the counter where the big cat stood.
Dried-fish crumbs on the counter under the cat's raised paw, in a small tidy trail toward the cat bed.
Red herring: Minho's backpack holds open packets with the very same crumbs, so Jina's case points straight at her own cousin.
The wind chime over the red door rings at night, but the door is bolted — the only other way in is the back-room cat flap.
Small claw scuffs on the crate, at exactly cat height.
premise.want: To catch the lucky cat's mover in the act.
premise.obstacle: Nabi only moves the cat when nobody is looking.
premise.clock: Before nine in the morning, when Halmoni unlocks the shop and finds the cat moved again — that is when the blame lands on Minho.
premise.normalDay: Every day after school, Jina works along the shelves with her magnifier and Minho eats his way along the snack shelf while Halmoni straightens her big lucky cat and slips Nabi a dried fish.
premise.whyToday: This morning the big cat was found turned to the wall, and only Minho was alone in the shop last night, so Halmoni blamed him and told him not to come back.
premise.whyCare: Minho is blamed for something he did not do, and Jina steps in front of him to say so and hands him half her snack before she starts the case.
spine: Once upon a time, in a small shop on a busy Seoul street, Halmoni kept a big lucky cat on the counter, its paw raised at the door to wave the luck in.

Every day after school Jina checked the lucky cats with her magnifier and Minho ate along the snack shelf, and every morning Halmoni found the big cat sitting somewhere new, and was sure it walked at night.
Until one day she found it turned to the wall, and because Minho had been alone in the shop the night before, she blamed him and told him not to come back.

Because of that, Jina had until nine the next morning to catch the real mover, so she smuggled Minho in and they hid behind the counter after closing — and while they argued about crumbs, Nabi came through the cat flap, climbed the crate an

Until finally the crate went over and the shelf of lucky cats came down, and Halmoni ran in to find the cousins in a sea of cats and Nabi up on the counter licking dried fish off the big cat's raised paw.

Ever since then the big cat faces the door by day and Nabi turns it to the wall by night, which is exactly how she makes Halmoni come over and open the dried-fish tin — and Minho is never blamed again; he is the shop's official snack-taster
